families.why: Only family with any feasible designs so far (39/53 feasible, and every one of the 12 designs on the merged front). The spec's binding constraints are accuracy (max_abs_err <= 2^-12) and the burst constraint (32 results in 0.5 us), and a 1-result/cycle pipelined unit with N+2 latency clears the burst easily at its Fmax. So this is where the area-vs-accuracy trade-off actually lives and where hypervolume is won or lost. Ranges: data_width 12..22 and n_iter 8..22 bracket both ends of the front - the min-area feasible corner needs W just large enough that the 2^-(W-2) output LSB plus rounding does not exceed 2^-12, while W/N up to ~22 supplies the high-accuracy_bits end that the HV reference (accuracy 12) rewards without pushing area past the area reference point. angle_guard -2..3 and frac_guard 0..3 let the search buy accuracy with guard bits instead of full data_width when that is cheaper, and negative angle_guard is the cheapest area lever if accuracy survives. rounding trunc|round is nearly free to try and round is worth several bits of LSB error.

Still 0/47 feasible, so it is either dead or it was searched in the wrong corner. It computes the same bits as pipelined for the same accuracy parameters, so the error constraint cannot be what kills it; the plausible failure mode is Fmax (and hence the 0.5 us / 32-result burst budget) collapsing as m grows, since m micro-rotations sit in one combinational path. That points at small m, not the whole 2..8 range, so I restrict m to 2..4 and keep data_width/n_iter in the low-to-mid band (13..20 / 8..20) where area - its only reason to exist - is smallest. If registering every 2-3 stages keeps Fmax high enough to still fit latency+31 cycles inside 0.5 us, pipelined_m with m=2-3 would have fewer pipeline FFs than pipelined at the same W/N and could take the min-area selection; that upside is worth ~1/3 of the round. If this share returns 0 feasible again, drop the family and put the remaining round into full-range pipelined front mapping.

parsed.rationale: The merged front is 100% pipelined and pipelined is 39/53 feasible, so the front I must cover is a pipelined area-vs-accuracy curve; most of the budget goes there. The selection rule is min area_um2 under max_abs_err <= 2^-12 and the 32-results-per-0.5-us burst bound, so I want dense coverage of the small-area feasible corner (the likely winner) plus enough of the higher-W/N accuracy region to fill the hypervolume box out to the area reference point. pipelined_m gets a smaller share purely as a bounded probe at small m, where it could undercut pipelined on area if it meets the burst bound; it has shown nothing yet, so I cap its share and will reallocate if it stays infeasible.
